proof_scope: Herdr runtime backend support for Tau-owned headless agent-node worker endpoints

claims.does_not_prove: Provider semantic quality, paid-provider execution, React Flow rendering, GOAL.md completion, or that the shipped adapter persists endpoint leases itself for restart adoption (the harness persists the lease record the scheduler needs; FakeProvider is the model in both workers).
claims.proves: A real Tau scheduler process is SIGKILLed while a Herdr-hosted worker is in flight and a restarted scheduler adopts the same endpoint from the durable lease record with one settlement and no duplicate endpoint or attempt; replacement_decision blocks on a live induced UNKNOWN observation and creates zero endpoints; the same fixture work order yields field-equal work orders and settlements (all fields except attempt_id/sha256, including turn/tool receipt digests, evidence, and journal head) through the local in-process path and the adapter's Herdr worker path; pane text is diagnostic only; an operator action round-trips through Tau's inbox; confirmed-dead retry gets new lineage; cleanup refuses foreign authorization and leaves an unrelated workspace pane intact; the installed wheel imports the adapter and backend without the source checkout.

what_was_exercised: local commands declared in the fixture manifest
what_remains_unverified: semantic correctness, live services, LLM judge behavior, and release readiness

claims.description: Tau-owned headless agent-node workers can run through the live Herdr runtime backend as exact leased endpoints while Tau retains endpoint ownership, observation, worker settlement receipts, and cleanup authority.

cases.name: live-herdr-scheduler-kill-unknown-liveness-and-local-equivalence
